thread.title: Dow Drops 600 Points Because Big Tech Can't Get Its Act Together

title: Dow Drops 600 Points Because Big Tech Can't Get Its Act Together
text:
Dow Drops 600 Points Because Big Tech Can’t Carry the Load By Dec. 27, 2018 2:26 p.m. ET Order Reprints Illustration by Michael Haddad Text size
2:07 p.m. Healthy markets don’t gain 5% in one day, which was one reason we predicted more volatility for the Dow Jones Industrial Average after it gained 1086 points in a single day .
Still, we never thought it would give back more than half those gains the very next day. The Dow has dropped 603.40 points, or 2.6%, to 22,275.05, while the S&P 500 has fallen 2.8% to 2,398.52, and the Nasdaq Composite has slumped 3.2% to 6,342.99.
As that 3% drop in the Nasdaq implies, one of the market’s big problems continues to be the lack of follow-through in Facebook (FB), Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), Netflix (NFLX) and Alphabet (GOOGL)--the FAANGs. Those stocks aren’t just some of the most popular, but also some of the market’s biggest. When they rally , as they did yesterday, they can pull the market up with them. But when they fall, as they are doing today, they drag the major indexes down with them. Facebook has fallen 2.7%, Alphabet has dropped 3.3%, Apple has slumped 4.3%, Netflix has tumbled 4.4%, and Amazon is off 5%.
Yet despite today’s decline, investors at least know where support is for now. For the S&P 500, it is at yesterday’s low of 2346.58, a level that is just above the 2344.60 that would signal the benchmark has officially sunk into a bear market. “The market was in full price discovery mode until buyers finally cared yesterday, and now that low (2,346.58) needs to be respected,” writes Instinet’s Frank Cappelleri. “Let’s hope so...the SPX still has a lot to do before the big, bad top gets negated.”
